profile: SQLite 3.47.2, UTF-8, stock VFS and PRAGMA implementation, native hexadecimal integer input, explicit attached-schema coordinates. A caller can impose additional connection restrictions.
scope: The 18 stock FLAG pragmas active in the pinned Linux and Darwin SQLite builds. Other built-in names and compile-time variants are listed independently in sqlite-pragma-namespace-v1.json.

Maintenance/FlagPragma.role: Read a native connection flag, request to turn it on or off, or clear writable_schema and reload the schema cache.
Maintenance/FlagPragma.structure: Exact FlagName, optional FlagChange, optional resolved schema Identifier.
Maintenance/FlagPragma.conditions: An explicit schema qualifier must resolve in SQLite's schema namespace before publication. The schema qualifies the native invocation without making its flag state schema-local. Reset is available only for writable_schema.
Maintenance/FlagPragma.meaning: One typed, canonically named integer row on read. A write requests the named transition at prepare time and returns no fields or rows. A foreign_keys write inside a transaction leaves the flag unchanged. Disabling defer_foreign_keys clears the deferred immediate-constraint counter. Reset also reloads the schema cache. Changes expire prepared statements and update affected pager flags.
Maintenance/FlagPragma.externalInterpretation: Use the same SQLite build, selected connection and attached databases, runtime flags, transaction state, defensive-mode restrictions and native prepared-statement behavior. Explicit temp selection opens the temp database. No custom VFS supplies extensions to these names.
Maintenance/FlagPragma.sql: Emit PRAGMA, the separately quoted database coordinate when supplied, the canonical name, and one of no suffix, = 0, = 1 or = RESET.

Maintenance/FlagName.role: Identify the exact built-in native connection setting.
Maintenance/FlagName.structure: Closed enum with the 18 active names from the independently extracted native FLAG family.
Maintenance/FlagName.conditions: Recognize a name using native ASCII case-insensitive comparison. Use the canonical enum name in the result header on reads.
Maintenance/FlagName.meaning: Selects the named SQLite flag and any native side effects associated with it.
Maintenance/FlagName.externalInterpretation: The pinned names map to the native flag masks in the independent pragma namespace. A debug-only compile-time name does not have a value in this enum.

Maintenance/FlagChange.role: Describe the native change requested by a pragma argument.
Maintenance/FlagChange.structure: Closed enum with Disable, Enable and Reset.
Maintenance/FlagChange.conditions: Only the parent writable_schema operation accepts Reset. Resolve the native argument interpretation before a complete value exists.
Maintenance/FlagChange.meaning: A stock native boolean setting, or the distinct request to clear writable_schema and reload the connection's schema cache.
Maintenance/FlagChange.externalInterpretation: Native flags may be affected by documented connection settings and transaction state.

rules: The native boolean argument recognizes on, yes and true using ASCII case-insensitive equality. Other text requests false except for Reset on writable_schema. A quoted sign or leading whitespace is part of the argument. A grammar PLUS on a number is discarded and a grammar MINUS is prepended.

When the decoded argument starts with a digit, read the decimal or 0x-prefixed hexadecimal integer prefix. Ignore following characters. A value outside the positive signed 32-bit magnitude maps to zero. After reducing a valid result to its low byte, nonzero means true. This is the native text rule even for an unquoted REAL or over-wide hexadecimal token.

Foreign key changes are a runtime state transition: setting foreign_keys during an explicit transaction does not toggle the flag. Setting or clearing writable_schema follows native defensive-mode restrictions.

Writable_schema Reset clears the bit and refreshes the connection catalog; a false boolean value alone leaves the loaded catalog intact. A freshly created table fixture with a deliberately renamed schema row distinguishes the two operations.

The optional resolved database coordinate preserves database selection and the native access to temp. Boolean arguments are semantic settings under the stock VFS and native authorization; unnormalized authorizer input text is not a statement result.
observations: Compare exact native flags, written/read result names, positions, integer storage class, rows, parameter shape, readOnly classification and connection state. Observe prepare-time values and visible schema attachment slots.

Use separately established witness SQL for changed rows, write restrictions, foreign key and CHECK enforcement, output labels, cursor traversal, recursive triggers and schema-cache reload. Preserve evaluation errors for fixed known effect probes.

Observe the native authorizer operation name, existing schema and presence of the argument. No assertion relies on SQL accepted by a candidate parser alone. The recorded raw argument remains available for review.

finite.identity: The full 864 flag/action/scope/baseline/transaction product plus the 16 Reset combinations. Derive identity from constructed fields, observed native scope, baseline and transaction.

exploration.domain: Vary flag, operation, qualifier, attached name and its escaping, casing, argument spelling, baseline and transaction. Traverse a separate pinned set of signed, decimal, hexadecimal, quoted, real, text and boundary witnesses.

negative: Direct Reset on a flag other than writable_schema
Direct unknown or mutable flag role
Unknown native PRAGMA name, which would otherwise be a silent no-op
Native rejection of numeric separators in the PRAGMA value grammar
faults: Allow Reset for the wrong flag
Drop the argument and read instead
Treat integer 256 as true instead of reducing to a byte
open: Debug flags, additional build profiles, custom VFS or argument-sensitive authorizer extensions, and all non-FLAG pragmas remain separately accounted for.

The independent effect probes exercise selected SQL-visible consequences. Filesystem sync, locking visibility, planner decisions, resource use, custom extensions and defensive mode need additional external evidence.
trust: Pinned native PRAGMA definition table and compiler profile.
Native action authorization restricted to the stock flag names in disposable connections.
Independent transition and observation model and the exact distributed implementation digest.
